subject.title: [Feature]: First-class multi-instance management for Docker installs

question: Should OpenClaw core own first-class Docker instance create/list/delete/update commands, or should multi-instance Docker remain a documented manual Compose/profile workflow for now?
rationale: The request defines new official operator UX and lifecycle semantics across Docker, config/state/workspace roots, ports, Compose naming, updates, deletion, and sandbox boundaries; current source inspection shows no existing implementation to clean up automatically.

options.title: Sponsor a minimal core design
options.body: Approve a narrow core design for named Docker instances, with explicit identity, persistence, port, update/delete, docs, and sandbox-isolation contracts before implementation.

options.title: Keep manual primitives for now
options.body: Leave the issue open as design backlog while relying on current multi-gateway docs, env variables, Compose, Docker setup, and ClawDock helpers.

options.title: Route to external wrapper first
options.body: Ask contributors to maintain a wrapper or ClawHub package around current primitives unless they identify a missing core API that blocks external implementation.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a minimal core design
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow core design for named Docker instances, with explicit identity, persistence, port, update/delete, docs, and sandbox-isolation contracts before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current history points most strongly to this owner for the multi-gateway guide and Docker setup surface that would frame the product decision.
